svg.text: final class · the only place rules live
package-private — the test seam for a fixed board ✓
every mutation short-circuits if status != IN_PROGRESS ✓
returns boolean "did it happen", never throws on a no-op
toggleFlag does NOT bounds-check — asymmetry, a real bug
no locks anywhere: one game = one player = one thread.
Board and Cell are plainly mutable; sharing a game across
threads would need a lock that is not written here.
STRATEGY — the only thing worth swapping
a fixed-layout impl makes every test deterministic
safeRow/safeCol in the signature = first-click safety is
a contract, not an implementation detail ✓
retry if it is the safe cell or already a mine
unseeded Random ⇒ NOT reproducible; no seed ctor
rejection loop degrades as mines → cells (Fisher-Yates fixes it)
THE GRID — Board owns every algorithm
minesPlaced: boolean — the "first click yet?" latch
revealBfs(r, c) — iterative flood fill, ArrayDeque queue
inBounds(r, c) — the single guard everything routes through
ctor rejects mineCount ≥ rows·cols — the one real invariant ✓
BFS is ITERATIVE — a 16×30 expert board would not blow the
stack, but recursion on a 1000×1000 grid would ✓
countRevealedSafeCells() rescans the WHOLE grid on every
move ⇒ win check is O(R·C) per reveal, not O(1).
Fix: keep a revealedSafe counter incremented in the BFS.
Board is the model AND the algorithm host. At this size that
is the right call — a separate FloodFiller for one method
would be ceremony, and the data it needs all lives here.
state as an enum, not a class
Minesweeper holds a GameStatus and can be built from a Difficulty preset

g.text: FIRST-CLICK SAFETY — and where it falls short
Mines are NOT placed at construction. The board sits empty
until the first reveal(), which calls placeMines(board, r, c)
and flips the minesPlaced latch. The clicked cell is excluded
from the draw, so move one can never lose.
Honest gap: only that ONE cell is excluded. Real Minesweeper
excludes the whole 3×3 neighbourhood so the first click always
opens a zero-region. Here the first click can legally land on
a "1" and reveal a single cell. Easy fix, worth naming out loud.
WHY LAZY MINE PLACEMENT AT ALL?
Because the safe cell is not known until the player picks it.
Any design that seeds mines in the constructor has to either
re-roll the whole board on an unlucky first click, or quietly
MOVE the mine the player hit — both are messier.
The latch also keeps the invariant single-shot: minesPlaced
flips exactly once, so adjacency counts are computed once
and never drift out of sync with the mine layout.
KNOWN LIMITATIONS — say these before the interviewer finds them
1. Two Difficulty enums exist: minesweeper/Difficulty (EASY/MEDIUM/HARD) is dead; model/Difficulty (BEGINNER/
INTERMEDIATE/EXPERT) is the one wired in. Delete the root one.
2. Cell exposes reveal()/placeMine()/toggleFlag() AND setRevealed()/setMine()/setFlagged(). Only the setters are used;
the verb methods are unreferenced. Two ways to do one thing is how state gets out of sync later.
3. No chording (middle-click on a satisfied number), no timer, no mine counter, no undo. All out of scope, on purpose.
4. Nothing is synchronized. That is fine for a single-player game and the right answer is to say so, not to sprinkle locks.
Naming your own gaps reads as senior. Being caught by them does not.
